target_customer: Aerospace engineering teams building drones, satellites and defense systems
problem: Aerospace teams spend long cycles designing, testing and simulating control systems and flight software. Elodin offers GPU physics simulation, cloud Monte Carlo runs, flight software and an open flight computer, pitched as CI/CD for aerospace.
business_model: Software licensing and cloud simulation plus hardware sales (Aleph flight computer); pricing not found
product_category: Aerospace simulation, flight software and flight computer hardware

founders.name: Daniel Driscoll
founders.background_notes: Background not on the sources opened.

founders.name: Sascha Wise
founders.background_notes: Background not on the sources opened.

competitors.name: Windhover Labs
competitors.what: Built on NASA cFS flight software for drones and sold flight computers, positioned as a US made alternative

technical_complexity.rationale: GPU physics simulation in Rust and Python on JAX, real-time telemetry and flight software with software and hardware in the loop testing, plus designing a Jetson based flight computer, is demanding for a team of five.

defensibility.rationale: Flight software and simulation integrate deeply into aerospace workflows and qualification, which raises switching costs, but open source options such as NASA cFS and F Prime exist.

incumbents: NASA cFS and F Prime (open source)
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy of Elodin was found.

market_need_then: Growth in small satellites and drones increased demand for faster simulation and flight software, and a 2024 paper cited gaps in the open source cFS and F Prime frameworks.

identity.voice_and_tone: technical aerospace engineering; pitched as CI/CD for Aerospace

branding.brand_signature: CI/CD for Aerospace and an open source flight computer named Aleph
branding.community_and_virality: Open source flight computer and simulation tooling; no independent brand press found.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear tagline and open source products appeal to engineers, but no press or community evidence about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Elodin is an active, five person YC Winter 2024 company selling simulation, flight software and a flight computer to aerospace teams. Aggregators report about 2M USD of early funding and its site shows customers such as NASA, but no primary funding announcement, later round or exit was found. Outcome is unclear.
notes: Aggregators (VCBacked, Extruct, Signalbase, CB Insights) report a 2M USD pre-seed around February 2024 with Y Combinator, Soma Capital, Karman Ventures, Kulveer Taggar and Leonis Investissement; totals range from 2.5M to 2.61M and conflict; no primary announcement found, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Founder backgrounds were not on any opened source. Customer logos are read from image file names on the company site, so unverified as paying customers. Competitor Windhover Labs is dated 2021, about two years before founding, the nearest dated source found. No Series A found.
